question: Which feature best distinguishes an acute leukemia from a chronic leukemia?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the morphologic and clinical differences between acute and chronic leukemia

options.rationale: Acute leukemias contain precursors with reduced capacity to differentiate, producing accumulation of immature blasts.
Preserved maturation characterizes chronic leukemia and would be correct if cells at multiple maturation stages predominated.
Discrete nodal or extranodal masses characterize lymphoma and would be correct for a mass-forming lymphoid neoplasm.
Indolent mature lymphocytes characterize chronic lymphoid neoplasms and would be correct for hairy cell leukemia.
Retained lineage development is a chronic leukemia feature and would be correct when the neoplastic cells remain capable of maturation.

question: A hematopoietic neoplasm diffusely involves bone marrow, and neoplastic cells are usually present in peripheral blood. Which term best classifies this growth pattern?
cited_learning_objective: Briefly review hematopoiesis and terminology (lymphoma, leukemia, myeloproliferative neoplasm)

options.rationale: Lymphoma forms discrete masses and would be correct if nodal or extranodal tumors predominated without widespread marrow involvement.
Leukemia is defined by widespread marrow involvement with tumor cells usually entering the peripheral blood.
Myeloid sarcoma is an extramedullary mass of myeloblasts and would be correct if a localized tumor outside marrow were described.
Thymic lymphoma produces a mediastinal mass and would be correct for the characteristic mass presentation of T-lineage disease.
This identifies a lineage and maturation category rather than the diffuse marrow-and-blood growth pattern described.

question: Which surface marker combination identifies the T-cell lineage of an acute lymphoblastic neoplasm?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: CD19 with CD10 supports B-lineage disease and would be correct for most B-ALL cases.
CD11c and CD25 occur in hairy cell leukemia and would be correct for a mature B-cell tumor with hairy projections.
CD3 and CD7 establish T-cell lineage in T-ALL.
CD103 is associated with hairy cell leukemia, while the combination does not define the T-cell lineage.
CD25 and CD103 support hairy cell leukemia and would be correct with an indolent mature B-cell presentation.

question: Which chromosomal abnormality creates the characteristic fusion protein in acute promyelocytic leukemia?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: t(12;21) produces ETV6::RUNX1 and would be correct for a favorable childhood B-ALL abnormality.
t(9;22) produces BCR::ABL1 and would be correct for Philadelphia chromosome-positive B-ALL.
t(8;21) produces RUNX1::RUNX1T1 and would be correct for another favorable AML subgroup.
inv(16) produces CBFB::MYH11 and would be correct for a favorable recurrent-genetic-abnormality AML.
t(15;17) creates PML::RARA, which blocks differentiation at the promyelocyte stage.

question: A marrow specimen contains 24% immature hematopoietic cells that cannot complete differentiation. Molecular analysis shows both transcription-factor dysregulation and increased tyrosine-kinase signaling. Which disease category best fits these findings?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the morphologic and clinical differences between acute and chronic leukemia

options.rationale: An acute leukemia combines a differentiation block with proliferative signaling and ordinarily meets a ≥20% blast threshold.
Chronic leukemias retain maturation and would be correct if differentiated cells at multiple stages predominated.
An indolent mature B-cell neoplasm would fit hairy cell leukemia, not a blast-rich process with blocked differentiation.
Lymphoma would require a discrete nodal or extranodal mass rather than a diffuse blast-rich marrow process.
A mature myeloid proliferation would retain differentiation and would be correct for a chronic myeloid pattern.

question: Two blast populations have indistinguishable appearances on routine microscopy. One is B-lineage and the other is myeloid. Which study most directly resolves this distinction?
cited_learning_objective: Brief overview of the 2016 revision to the World Health Organization (WHO) classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia

options.rationale: Morphology cannot reliably separate lymphoblasts from myeloblasts and would suffice only if lineage-specific structures were evident.
Flow cytometry uses surface-antigen expression to establish lineage when blast morphology is nondiagnostic.
Reticulin staining evaluates marrow fibrosis and would support hairy cell leukemia when aspiration produces a dry tap.
Phase contrast microscopy highlights hairy projections and would be useful for suspected hairy cell leukemia.
Marrow aspiration demonstrates blast abundance but does not reliably establish lymphoid versus myeloid lineage by itself.

question: An immature hematopoietic tumor is TdT-positive and expresses CD19 and CD10. Which classification is most consistent with this profile?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: T-ALL is TdT-positive but expresses CD3 and CD7 rather than the B-lineage markers in this profile.
AML is a myeloid blast neoplasm and would be supported by myeloperoxidase positivity or Auer rods.
TdT establishes lymphoid immaturity, while CD19 and CD10 support B-lineage differentiation.
Monocytic differentiation is associated with folded nuclei and nonspecific esterase positivity rather than CD19 and CD10.
Hairy cell leukemia is a mature B-cell neoplasm and would express CD11c, CD25, CD103, and annexin A1.

question: A childhood B-lineage acute leukemia has a low presenting leukocyte count and a chromosomal abnormality associated with favorable outcome. Which genetic finding is most consistent?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: KMT2A rearrangement is unfavorable and would fit an infant or other high-risk presentation.
BCR::ABL1 is an unfavorable finding and would be more characteristic of adult B-ALL.
FLT3-ITD is an unfavorable AML marker and would be correct in a myeloid rather than B-lymphoblastic neoplasm.
ETV6::RUNX1 results from t(12;21), the most common childhood B-ALL translocation, and predicts favorable outcome.
TP53 mutation is an unfavorable AML marker and would be correct in an adverse-risk myeloid neoplasm.

question: An adult B-lineage acute leukemia contains a constitutively active enzyme that increases proliferation and worsens prognosis. Which molecular alteration is most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: ETV6::RUNX1 is favorable and would fit a common childhood B-ALL rather than adverse adult disease.
PML::RARA blocks promyelocyte differentiation and would be correct for acute promyelocytic leukemia.
CBFB::MYH11 is a favorable AML abnormality and would fit inv(16)-associated myeloid disease.
NPM1 mutation without FLT3-ITD is favorable in AML and does not define the proliferative enzyme described.
BCR::ABL1 is a constitutively active tyrosine kinase, is common in adult B-ALL, and predicts an unfavorable outcome.

question: A myeloid blast population contains rod-shaped aggregates formed from fused azurophilic granules. Which additional finding should accompany this differentiation pattern?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: Auer rods indicate myeloid differentiation, and myeloblasts are myeloperoxidase-positive.
Nonspecific esterase positivity supports monoblasts, which characteristically lack Auer rods.
TRAP positivity supports hairy cell leukemia and would be correct for mature cells with cytoplasmic projections.
TdT positivity indicates lymphoid immaturity and would be correct for most lymphoblastic leukemias.
Annexin A1 supports hairy cell leukemia and would be correct for an indolent mature B-cell neoplasm.

question: A myeloid neoplasm develops 2 years after treatment with etoposide and was not preceded by a myelodysplastic phase. Which molecular event best matches this pattern?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: PML::RARA defines APL and would be correct if abnormal promyelocytes with numerous Auer rods predominated.
Topoisomerase II inhibitors produce DNA breaks near KMT2A, with misrepair causing partner-gene fusions after a 1-3 year latency.
BRAF V600E drives hairy cell leukemia and would be correct for an indolent mature B-cell neoplasm.
ETV6::RUNX1 characterizes favorable childhood B-ALL rather than short-latency therapy-related AML.
CBFB::MYH11 defines favorable inv(16) AML but is not the characteristic event after topoisomerase II inhibition.

question: A treatment-associated myeloid neoplasm appears 6 years after exposure and follows a preceding dysplastic marrow disorder. Which exposure pattern is most consistent?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: Topoisomerase II inhibitors produce a 1-3 year latency without a preceding myelodysplastic phase.
Benzene is an AML risk factor but does not define the characteristic treatment-latency pattern described.
Purine analogs treat hairy cell leukemia and are not the treatment-associated AML pattern presented.
Alkylating-agent-associated AML typically has a 5-7 year latency and is often preceded by myelodysplasia.
All-trans retinoic acid treats APL by restoring differentiation and is not the causal exposure described.

question: A mature B-cell neoplasm activates a serine/threonine kinase and can later be treated by inhibiting that same altered protein. Which abnormality provides both diagnostic and therapeutic information?
cited_learning_objective: Brief overview of the 2016 revision to the World Health Organization (WHO) classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia

options.rationale: BRAF V600E occurs in more than 90% of hairy cell leukemias and serves as both a diagnostic marker and drug target.
FLT3-ITD is an adverse AML marker and would be correct for a targetable myeloid blast neoplasm.
TP53 mutation predicts unfavorable AML but is not the characteristic diagnostic and therapeutic marker of this mature B-cell tumor.
NPM1 mutation contributes to AML risk classification and would be favorable when FLT3-ITD is absent.
KMT2A rearrangement is associated with adverse acute leukemia and short-latency topoisomerase II inhibitor-related AML.

question: An immature leukemia has scant basophilic cytoplasm, frequent mitoses, and macrophages containing apoptotic debris. Which finding most directly establishes precursor lymphoid differentiation?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: Auer rods establish myeloid differentiation and would be correct for myeloblasts.
Myeloperoxidase positivity supports myeloblasts and would establish myeloid rather than lymphoid lineage.
TdT is expressed in more than 95% of ALL cases and identifies immature lymphoid cells.
Nonspecific esterase positivity supports monocytic differentiation and would be correct for monoblasts.
TRAP positivity supports hairy cell leukemia and would be correct for a mature B-cell process.

question: A recurrent genetic abnormality is detected in a patient whose marrow contains 14% myeloid blasts. Which finding permits classification as acute myeloid leukemia despite the subthreshold blast percentage?
cited_learning_objective: Brief overview of the 2016 revision to the World Health Organization (WHO) classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia

options.rationale: BRAF V600E supports hairy cell leukemia and does not create the specified blast-count exception.
FLT3-ITD is an adverse AML marker but does not independently permit diagnosis below the usual blast threshold.
TP53 mutation predicts unfavorable AML and would not by itself override the blast-count requirement.
KMT2A rearrangement is adverse but is not among the stated abnormalities permitting diagnosis regardless of blast count.
PML::RARA from t(15;17) permits AML classification regardless of blast count.

question: A 4-year-old child develops abrupt fatigue, fever, bruising, and refusal to walk. Examination shows generalized lymph-node enlargement. Which diagnosis best integrates the marrow-failure and infiltration findings?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: B-ALL peaks near age 3 and produces marrow failure, bone pain, and generalized tissue infiltration.
T-ALL typically affects adolescent males with a thymic mass and would be correct if mediastinal compression dominated.
Monocytic AML more characteristically infiltrates skin and gums and would be correct with leukemia cutis or gingival hypertrophy.
APL usually affects younger or middle-aged adults and would be correct with coagulopathy and abnormal promyelocytes.
Hairy cell leukemia is an indolent disease of middle-aged men and would be correct with massive splenomegaly and monocytopenia.

question: A 16-year-old boy has progressive dyspnea and facial venous congestion. Imaging shows an anterior mediastinal mass, and blood contains TdT-positive blasts. Which lineage markers are most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: CD19 and CD10 support B-ALL, which usually presents as childhood acute leukemia rather than a thymic mass.
An adolescent male with a thymic mass has the characteristic presentation of T-ALL, which expresses CD3 and CD7.
CD11c and CD25 support hairy cell leukemia and would be correct with splenomegaly, pancytopenia, and hairy lymphocytes.
CD25 and CD103 are hairy cell markers and do not identify the precursor T-cell tumor described.
CD103 supports hairy cell leukemia, while precursor T-lineage disease requires CD3 and CD7.

question: A 6-year-old receiving systemic therapy for B-lineage acute leukemia enters marrow remission. The treatment team adds site-directed prophylaxis because one compartment is poorly reached by systemic drugs. Which site is being targeted?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: The spleen may be infiltrated but is not identified as the compartment requiring routine prophylaxis.
The liver may enlarge from infiltration but is not the poorly penetrated site requiring standard prophylaxis.
The CNS is a sanctuary site poorly reached by systemic chemotherapy, so CNS prophylaxis is required.
Lymph nodes can be infiltrated but are not the sanctuary compartment targeted by standard prophylaxis.
Subperiosteal infiltration causes bone pain but is not identified as a sanctuary site requiring prophylaxis.

question: A 38-year-old with B-lineage acute leukemia has t(9;22). Standard aggressive chemotherapy is initiated. Which additional treatment most directly addresses the adverse molecular driver?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: All-trans retinoic acid degrades PML::RARA and would be correct for acute promyelocytic leukemia.
Arsenic trioxide targets PML::RARA and would be correct in APL rather than Philadelphia-positive B-ALL.
Cladribine treats hairy cell leukemia and would be correct for an indolent mature B-cell neoplasm.
t(9;22) creates BCR::ABL1, so adding a tyrosine kinase inhibitor such as imatinib targets the proliferative driver.
Vemurafenib inhibits mutant BRAF and would be correct for refractory hairy cell leukemia.

question: A 3-year-old with B-lineage acute leukemia has a leukocyte count of 28,000/µL [4,500-11,000/µL] and hyperdiploid blasts. Which prognostic category best fits this presentation?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: Age 2-10 years, a count below 50,000/µL, and hyperdiploidy are favorable features in ALL.
Infants younger than 2 years have adverse risk, often with KMT2A rearrangement; this child is older.
Adult presentation is adverse and would be correct if this disease occurred during adulthood.
Hypodiploidy or BCR::ABL1 would support adverse cytogenetic risk; hyperdiploidy is favorable.
Marked leukocytosis is adverse, while this count remains below the stated favorable threshold of 50,000/µL.

question: A 72-year-old develops fatigue, mucosal bleeding, and recurrent bacterial infections. Marrow evaluation shows accumulated immature myeloid cells caused by impaired differentiation. Which diagnosis is most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: B-ALL is composed of lymphoblasts and is most characteristic in childhood, although it can occur in adults.
AML predominantly affects adults, has a median diagnostic age of 70, and causes marrow failure through myeloid blast accumulation.
T-ALL typically presents in adolescent males with a mediastinal thymic mass.
Hairy cell leukemia is a mature indolent B-cell disease and would be supported by massive splenomegaly and monocytopenia.
APL would require promyelocytic differentiation, often with many Auer rods and disseminated intravascular coagulation.

question: A patient with acute myeloid leukemia has a leukocyte count of 145,000/µL [4,500-11,000/µL], confusion, and dyspnea with bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. Which mechanism best explains the acute organ dysfunction?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: AML blasts are large and poorly deformable, allowing hyperleukocytosis to produce leukostasis in cerebral and pulmonary vessels.
Erythroid suppression causes anemia and would be correct if fatigue and dyspnea occurred without the neurologic and infiltrative pattern.
Platelet suppression causes petechiae and mucosal bleeding rather than confusion with bilateral pulmonary infiltrates.
Splenic sequestration contributes to cytopenias in hairy cell leukemia and would be correct with massive splenomegaly.
Meningeal involvement can cause neurologic symptoms in ALL but does not explain the simultaneous pulmonary findings linked to hyperleukocytosis.

question: A patient with myeloid leukemia develops raised violaceous skin lesions and marked gingival enlargement. Which differentiation pattern most strongly predicts these tissue findings?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: Promyelocytic differentiation is associated with many Auer rods and coagulopathy rather than characteristic skin and gum infiltration.
AML with monocytic differentiation characteristically infiltrates skin and gums, causing leukemia cutis and gingival hypertrophy.
Megakaryoblastic leukemia is associated with young children with Down syndrome rather than the infiltration pattern described.
Erythroid differentiation is a rare AML pattern and is not the characteristic cause of skin and gum infiltration.
Lymphoblastic disease more often causes lymphadenopathy, organomegaly, or sanctuary-site disease rather than this monocytic pattern.

question: A patient with 12% marrow myeloid blasts has t(8;21). The laboratory initially declines an acute leukemia classification because the blast percentage is below 20%. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Brief overview of the 2016 revision to the World Health Organization (WHO) classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia

options.rationale: Chronic myeloid leukemia retains maturation and is associated with BCR::ABL1, not the defining abnormality presented.
Hairy cell leukemia is a BRAF-mutated mature B-cell neoplasm and does not fit this myeloid genetic finding.
Waiting is unnecessary because t(8;21) already establishes an AML-defining recurrent genetic abnormality.
t(8;21) is an exception to the 20% blast threshold, so AML is diagnosed regardless of blast count.
Myeloid sarcoma requires an extramedullary myeloblast mass, which is not described.

question: A 34-year-old presents with gingival bleeding and widespread bruising. Smear shows abnormal promyelocytes containing bundles of rod-shaped granules. Which immediate complication makes this condition a medical emergency?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: APL promyelocyte granules release procoagulants, making disseminated intravascular coagulation a common life-threatening complication.
CNS relapse is associated with the sanctuary-site behavior of ALL and would be correct after incomplete CNS-directed prophylaxis.
Superior vena cava syndrome results from a mediastinal T-ALL mass and would be correct with facial congestion and airway compression.
Atypical mycobacterial infection is associated with hairy cell leukemia and would be correct with monocytopenia.
Pulmonary leukostasis occurs with marked AML hyperleukocytosis and would be correct with dyspnea, infiltrates, and a count above 100,000/µL.

question: A 41-year-old has acute promyelocytic leukemia complicated by active coagulopathy. Molecular testing identifies the defining fusion. Which treatment mechanism directly reverses the maturation arrest?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: BCR::ABL1 inhibition treats Philadelphia-positive ALL and would be correct if t(9;22) were present.
Mutant BRAF inhibition treats refractory hairy cell leukemia and would be correct with BRAF V600E.
All-trans retinoic acid and arsenic trioxide degrade PML::RARA, allowing arrested promyelocytes to differentiate.
FLT3 inhibition targets FLT3-mutated AML and would be correct if that adverse molecular driver were identified.
KMT2A rearrangement characterizes adverse acute leukemia but is not the differentiation block targeted in APL.

question: A 56-year-old man has massive splenic enlargement, pancytopenia, and a marked reduction in circulating monocytes. Lymph-node enlargement is absent. Which diagnosis is most likely?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: B-ALL has an abrupt presentation with lymphoblasts and often generalized lymphadenopathy rather than characteristic monocytopenia.
T-ALL typically causes a mediastinal mass in adolescent males rather than this indolent splenic presentation.
Monocytic AML often infiltrates skin and gums and does not characteristically produce monocytopenia.
APL typically presents with bleeding from disseminated intravascular coagulation and abnormal promyelocytes.
Hairy cell leukemia classically affects middle-aged men and causes massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia, monocytopenia, and little lymphadenopathy.

question: A patient with massive splenic enlargement and monocytopenia undergoes marrow aspiration, but no specimen can be obtained. Which pathologic process most directly explains this result?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: Hairy cells become enmeshed in marrow reticulin fibrils, producing fibrosis and a dry aspiration.
Promyelocyte granules cause disseminated intravascular coagulation and would be correct for APL-associated bleeding.
Vascular obstruction causes leukostasis and would be correct with AML hyperleukocytosis, confusion, and pulmonary infiltrates.
Subperiosteal infiltration causes bone pain in ALL but does not explain a dry marrow aspiration.
Monoblast infiltration causes leukemia cutis and gingival hypertrophy rather than aspiration failure.

question: A 58-year-old man with an indolent mature B-cell leukemia has pancytopenia and splenomegaly. Peripheral cells have fuzzy cytoplasmic extensions. Which initial treatment is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: Imatinib targets BCR::ABL1 and would be correct for Philadelphia-positive B-ALL.
Hairy cell leukemia is exceptionally sensitive to purine analogs such as cladribine or pentostatin.
All-trans retinoic acid treats PML::RARA-positive APL by restoring promyelocyte differentiation.
Arsenic trioxide degrades PML::RARA and would be correct as part of APL therapy.
Intensive chemotherapy is used for acute leukemias, whereas this indolent tumor responds to gentler purine-analog therapy.

question: A patient with hairy cell leukemia initially responds to a purine analog but later has treatment failure. Molecular testing confirms the characteristic kinase alteration. Which next treatment best targets that abnormality?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: Imatinib targets BCR::ABL1 and would be correct for Philadelphia chromosome-positive B-ALL.
All-trans retinoic acid targets the differentiation block in APL and would be correct with PML::RARA.
Vemurafenib targets BRAF V600E and is used when conventional hairy cell leukemia chemotherapy fails.
Arsenic trioxide degrades PML::RARA and would be correct for acute promyelocytic leukemia.
FLT3 inhibitors target FLT3-mutated AML and would be correct if that myeloid alteration were present.

question: A 54-year-old man has an indolent leukemia with massive splenic enlargement and recurrent atypical mycobacterial infection. Which blood-cell abnormality most specifically contributes to this infectious pattern?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the clinical and pathological features of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, and hairy cell leukemia

options.rationale: Reduced erythrocytes cause anemia and would explain fatigue rather than the characteristic infectious susceptibility.
Reduced platelets cause bleeding and would be correct if petechiae or mucosal hemorrhage predominated.
Lymphoblast reduction is not the characteristic blood abnormality in hairy cell leukemia.
Monocytopenia is characteristic of hairy cell leukemia and accompanies susceptibility to infections including atypical mycobacteria.
Promyelocytes accumulate in APL; their reduction does not explain the infectious pattern described.
